limitations: Back-to-back calls measure coverage and endpoint latency, not an installed one-minute scheduler or a load/soak guarantee.
Observed workload is nine deployments with two or three unique instances each; expected larger-workload figures are projections.
Extension simulations include healthy entries. A no-op extension is not a future rent estimate; the runner acts only at the due threshold.
Four public TESTNET contract instances were genuinely restored; code entries were already live. No public expired-code restoration or invocation/payment-after-restoration was exercised.
Fee measurements are TESTNET observations. No mainnet budget is established or production activation authorized.
Successful due extension by the deployed cron and the actual browser/factory/wallet journey remain release checks; current shared Subscription/Webhook hashes were not activated.
The separate channel/lease follow-up proves both channel cases and held-lease blocking; injected failing inventory targets and long-run lease renewal remain untested in this environment.
